components.label: Note
components.summary: A short Markdown note: the question, a procedure, or a concept explanation. Keep it under ~120 words.

actions.editCondition: {nodeId, condition}: replace a filter condition (prefer the edit_node tool, which asks the student first)
actions.probe: {nodeId, value}: test one value against a filter node
actions.run: {}: run the program and replay its trace

fields.error: runCompleted: the Python exception type, or null
fields.keeps.*: editCondition: for each probe value, whether the new condition keeps it (true/false/"error")
fields.ok: runCompleted: the run finished without an error
fields.value.*: runCompleted: final value of a top-level name, as a Python repr (e.g. "10.0")

probeValues.description: Values the student can drag onto a filter node

source.description: The program; node ids are the names it assigns

components.label: Code graph
components.summary: Python source shown as a data-flow graph derived from it (the source stays the truth). The student drags test values onto filter nodes, edits a filter condition, and runs the code. Supports a small Python subset: assignments, list literals, list comprehensions with `if`, def/return, sum/len/print, arithmetic and comparisons, `is (not) None`.

actions.setDistance: {distance}: move the second particle to this distance (nm)

range.description: [min, max] distance in nm the student can reach

components.label: Force lab
components.summary: Two particles drawn on the canvas; the student drags either one and sees the net force along the line between them. The force comes from key points you give (interpolated locally), so label it ai-estimate.

components.label: Readout
components.summary: Live force, distance and F(r) chart of the force lab with the same experimentId.

actions.dispenseTo: {volume, mode: "stream" | "dropwise"}: run titrant in to this burette reading
actions.newTrial: {}: refill the flask (throws the current attempt away; the student is asked first)

fields.mixed: false while unmixed titrant is still in the flask
fields.overshoot: recordEndpoint: reading minus the equivalence volume
fields.toEquivalence: mL left to the equivalence point

transition.description: [low, high] pH of the colour change

components.label: Titration rig
components.summary: An acid–base titration rig: a burette of titrant over a flask of analyte with an indicator. The student turns the tap, swirls the flask by shaking it, records the endpoint and starts new trials. Ideal strong acid / strong base model.

components.label: Lab readout
components.summary: Burette reading, pH, flask colour, pH–volume curve and recorded trials of the titration rig with the same experimentId.

also.description: Another name shown as a note

components.label: Result
components.summary: A small table of results. Either fixed rows, or `compareRuns` to show the last two runs of the code graph in the same experiment (give both the same experimentId) side by side.

electrons.description: n in M^n+ + n e⁻ → M

solutionColor.description: CSS colour of the solution, e.g. "#2563eb" for Cu²⁺

components.label: Half-cell
components.summary: A beaker half-cell: a metal electrode in a solution of its ions, drawn as apparatus. Sockets: `electrode` (for meter leads) and `solution` (for salt-bridge ends). The student can dilute the solution tenfold or refill it. Its potential follows the Nernst equation at 25 °C.

fields.sameBeaker: both ends are in the same beaker

components.label: Salt bridge
components.summary: A salt bridge with two tube ends (plugs `a` and `b`, kind bridge). Dipping one end into each half-cell `solution` lets ions flow and closes the circuit.

actions.connect: {plug: "v" | "com" | "data", to: {objectId, port} | null}: clip a lead onto a half-cell `electrode`, or the cable into a log `in`

components.label: Voltmeter
components.summary: A digital voltmeter with a red lead `v` and a black lead `com` (kind lead) and a `data` cable (kind data). It shows E(red) − E(black) only when both leads are on electrodes of different half-cells joined by a salt bridge; otherwise 0.000 V, like a real meter.

fields.black: metal under the black lead, or null
fields.circuit: "unplugged" (a lead hangs free), "same-cell", "open" (no salt bridge between the two cells) or "closed"
fields.pair: the two metals, sorted and joined with "|", e.g. "Cu|Zn"
fields.red: metal under the red lead, or null

components.label: Lab notebook
components.summary: A lab notebook that records the reading of the meter whose data cable is plugged into its `in` socket. Pre-plug the cable with the scene's `wiring`.

actions.finish: {}: say the algorithm can stop now
actions.keep: {index}: leave that pair as it is
actions.resetSort: {}: back to the starting order (throws the attempt away; the student is asked first)
actions.swap: {index}: swap the pair at index and index + 1 (must be the pair the pass has reached)

fields.equal: swap/keep: the two values are equal (swapping them breaks stability)
fields.index: swap/keep: left index of the pair
fields.left: swap/keep: left value before the decision
fields.outOfOrder: swap/keep: left > right, so bubble sort swaps
fields.pass: swap/keep: the pass the decision belongs to
fields.passEnded: swap/keep: this decision finished the pass
fields.passSwaps: swap/keep: swaps so far in that pass
fields.right: swap/keep: right value before the decision
fields.sorted: finish: the values are in order
fields.verified: finish: the algorithm can know it is done (the last pass made no swaps, or every pass has run)

values.description: The starting order; repeat a value to discuss stability

components.label: Sort bench
components.summary: A row of values drawn as bars that the student sorts by hand with bubble sort: in the highlighted pair they drag one bar past the other to swap them, or drag the arrow under the pair on (or tap it) to keep them. A pass ends by itself at the values already in their final place (shown in green). Done says the algorithm can stop. The table lists each pass with its comparisons and swaps.

components.label: Code
components.summary: The sorting code, shown next to the sort bench with the same experimentId. As the student decides pairs on the bench it highlights the line that ran (compare, swap, the end-of-pass check or break) and shows i, j, swapped and the list.

actions.selectLine: {index}: light the tube with this lamp line
actions.setIntensity: {level}: 0.25 … 1 (moves the lamp to the matching distance)

fields.belowThreshold: this light frees no electrons at any intensity
fields.current: nA on the meter at the present voltage

lines.description: Lamp lines the student can pick

maxCurrent.description: nA at full intensity and no retarding voltage

components.label: Photoelectric rig
components.summary: A phototube lit by one line of a mercury lamp at a time, worked by hand: the student slides a selector along the spectrum to pick the line, slides the lamp along its rail (intensity goes as 1/d², from 1 at 10 cm to 0.25 at 20 cm), and turns a knob for the retarding voltage, reading the photocurrent on a nanoammeter. Its `data` plug carries the reading to a photo log `in` socket (pre-plug it with the scene `wiring`). Ideal model: V₀ = (hf − φ)/e, current falling linearly to zero at V₀, no current below the threshold frequency.

actions.recordStop: {}: record the voltage as V₀ for the lit line

fields.belowThreshold: recordStop: the light frees no electrons, so there is no V₀
fields.connected: recordStop: a rig is plugged in
fields.current: recordStop: nA on the meter (V₀ needs 0.0)
fields.overshoot: recordStop: recorded voltage minus the true V₀, V (large means the current was already zero lower down)
fields.points: fitLine: distinct frequencies in the fit
fields.repeatSame: recordStop: this line was already recorded at another intensity with the same V₀ (within 0.03 V)
fields.workFunction: fitLine: φ from the intercept, eV

components.label: Photo log
components.summary: A lab notebook for the photoelectric rig whose data cable is plugged into its `in` socket. Record V₀ stores the rig's present voltage as the stopping voltage of its line (only once the current reads 0.0 nA; recording the same line and intensity again replaces it). Fit line draws the least-squares line of V₀ against frequency and reports h = e × slope and the work function.

actions.choose: {option}: pick an answer by its index

components.label: Prediction
components.summary: A short multiple-choice question the student answers before experimenting, so a misconception shows up before it is tested. Write checks on `choose` for each option; the student can change their answer.

g.description: m/s², what the student is meant to find

components.label: Pendulum

gate.about: The lowest point of the swing, where a photogate clips on

components.summary: A simple pendulum on a stand, drawn as apparatus and always swinging. Everything is direct manipulation: the student pulls the bob sideways to set the release angle (2–60°), drags the pivot up or down to set the string length (0.20–1.50 m), and drags a 50, 100 or 200 g bob from the tray onto the string. Its `gate` socket (kind sensor) is the lowest point of the swing, where a photogate clips on. The period includes the large-amplitude correction, so readings above about 15° come out noticeably long.

components.label: Photogate timer
components.summary: A photogate timer. Its `gate` plug (kind sensor) clips onto a pendulum's `gate` socket at the bottom of the swing, and it then shows the period to the millisecond. Its `data` cable carries the reading to a pendulum log `in` socket (pre-plug it with the scene `wiring`).

actions.recordPeriod: {}: record the period the photogate shows

fields.connected: recordPeriod: a photogate is plugged in
fields.gated: recordPeriod: its sensor is clipped onto a pendulum
fields.largeAngle: fitG: some points were released above 15°
fields.sameOtherMass: recordPeriod: same length and angle already recorded with another mass, same period

components.label: Pendulum log
components.summary: A lab notebook for the photogate whose data cable is plugged into its `in` socket. Record T stores the period with the length, mass and release angle (recording the same length and mass again replaces the row, so a reading can be retaken at a smaller angle). Fit g draws T² against L and gives g = 4π² / slope.

Playground Canvas contracts.

Everything that crosses the boundary between the Canvas and its host (the demo shell today, the Athena tutor later) is defined here: scenes, objects, actions, links, checks, events, the canvas snapshot and the agent tools.

One action model drives everything. A student's gesture, an agent tool call and a demonstration replay all dispatch the same `Action`; every committed action is also an event on the event stream.

ObjectSpec.description: An object as a scene or the agent describes it. The Canvas decides its position.

PendulumConfig.description: A simple pendulum on a stand. Its lowest point is a `gate` socket where a photogate clips on. `g` is what the student is meant to find.

PendulumLogConfig.description: Records periods from the photogate plugged into it, and fits T² against L for g.

PhotoLogConfig.description: Records stopping voltages from the phototube plugged into it, and fits V₀ against frequency.

PhotoelectricConfig.description: A phototube lit by one line of a lamp at a time, with a retarding voltage and a nanoammeter. Its `data` cable carries the reading to a photo log.

PhotogateConfig.description: Times the pendulum its `gate` plug is clipped onto; the `data` cable carries the period.

PotentialLogConfig.description: Records readings from whatever instrument is plugged into it.

PredictConfig.description: A question the student answers before trying something, so the tutor knows what they expect.

Provenance.description: Where a piece of content comes from. The UI labels each one differently so that an AI estimate is never mistaken for a real run.

Relation.description: A small, fixed set of typed relations. Links are drawn, never executed.

compareRuns.description: Or compare the last two runs of the code graph in the same experiment, live.

rows.description: Fixed rows, e.g. values the scene already knows.

values.description: Final value of each top-level name, as Python reprs.

intro.description: The tutor's message when it opens the scene.

showMe.description: What the tutor does when the student asks to be shown the right way.

wiring.description: Plugs already attached when the scene opens, e.g. a meter's data cable into its log.

SortBenchConfig.description: A row of values the student sorts by hand, one comparison at a time. Each pass walks the pairs that aren't in their final place yet.

SortCodeConfig.description: The algorithm's source next to a sort bench in the same experiment. It highlights the line the hand trace has reached and shows the variables. `lines` are 1-based line numbers in `source`.

TitrationConfig.description: An acid–base titration rig: a burette of base over a flask of acid with an indicator. Concentrations are chosen when the scene is generated; pH and colour come from an ideal strong acid / strong base model computed locally.

TitrationReadoutConfig.description: Shows readings, recorded trials and the titration curve of the rig in the same experiment.

TutorResponse.description: A tutor turn prepared when the scene is generated: a chat message plus tool calls run in order (a demonstration finishes before the next call starts). The Canvas ignores these; the tutor runtime plays them back, so the common branches need no model call at all.

once.description: Answer only the first time (default true for checks).

then.description: Follow-up once the demonstration these calls start has finished, including one the student first had to accept (e.g. add a note explaining what they saw).

topic.description: Responses with the same topic aren't repeated back to back (default: the check id).

tools.description: Open the Playground with a scene: the goal, the objects (pick from the preset object types and fill in their config), typed links between them, and the checks including likely misconception branches.
tools.name: open_playground

tools.description: Read the canvas: objects with their current state, who changed them, feedback, selection and recent events.
tools.name: get_canvas_state

tools.description: Add one object near a related one. Do not give coordinates.
tools.name: add_object

tools.description: Change an object's config. If the student has changed that object, the student is asked to confirm first.
tools.name: update_config

tools.description: Draw a typed link between two objects.
tools.name: link

tools.description: Propose a structured edit to a code-graph node (its filter condition). The student sees a diff and accepts or rejects it.
tools.name: edit_node

tools.description: Replay actions with a visible virtual hand, e.g. drag a particle to a distance, run the code, or plug a lead into an electrode ({type:'connect', plug, to:{objectId, port}}). Uses the objects' own actions; give an action its own objectId to act on another object.
tools.name: demonstrate

tools.description: Draw attention to an object or one part of it (e.g. a node id).
tools.name: highlight
